title: When the Spire Falls Anew
premise: Gideon Delacroix, once a battle-priest of the silent god Veyra, discovers the old gods are answering prayers again because the last dragon, Ashenveil, is dying — and its fire is the wick that keeps divine voices lit. Hunted by the city's anti-magic inquisitors and shadowed by her former oath-brother Cassian, who now serves the inquisition, Gideon must reach the ruined Spire where the covenant between gods and mortals was first broken. There she learns her own forgotten memories hold the covenant's missing half: she was its final witness, and Veyra's silence was a sacrifice made to hide her. In the Spire's heart, Gideon chooses love over duty by refusing to relight the flame with her own life; instead she and Cassian reforge the covenant as equals, mortal and divine sharing the burden, and Ashenveil's last breath becomes a new dawn of quiet, shared magic rather than dominion.
about_author: Jude Okonkwo is a Nigerian-British writer who grew up between Lagos and Manchester, trading stories of trickster gods for rain-grey cities. A former archivist, they write fantasy about broken oaths, stubborn women, and the debts we inherit.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Selling smuggled charms in the outlaw-city of Corvane, Gideon feels her dead god stir when a child's prayer is suddenly answered with real fire. Inquisitors raid her stall; she escapes with help from an old client, but learns the answered prayers are spreading across the realm. Emotional beat: wary hope cracking open ten years of grief and numbness.

chapters.title: The Oath-Brother's Blade
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with one interlude from Cassian. Pursued toward the mountains, Gideon is cornered by Cassian, who hesitates at the killing stroke and instead reveals the inquisitors' true order: erase all witnesses to the old covenant — starting with her. Their fractured bond resurfaces as they flee together. Emotional beat: betrayal transmuted into reluctant trust, old love rekindling under threat.

chapters.title: What the Silence Was Hiding
chapters.summary: Climax. At the ruined Spire, dragon-fire guttering, Gideon recovers her sealed memories: Veyra went silent to conceal Gideon, the covenant's living witness, from those who would burn her to seize divine power alone. The inquisitor-archon arrives demanding exactly that sacrifice. Gideon refuses the choice she was fated for. Emotional beat: terror and fury resolving into defiant self-authorship.

chapters.title: A Covenant Reforged
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating Gideon and Cassian. Rather than one martyr, Gideon and Cassian offer a shared vow — mortals and gods bearing the flame together — and Ashenveil's last breath kindles a new, quieter covenant. Magic returns lawfully to Corvane; Veyra speaks Gideon's name once more. Emotional beat: grief finally laid down, love and duty reconciled as inheritance passed forward.
